payload.author: exam:3@run-18
payload.body:
examiner (exam-3): writing `tests/lint-ui.test.ts` as five `test` blocks, one per Proof leg, each named for its leg and its Machine clause.

Shape: one memoised probe writes the three temporary files under a single module-level random suffix — the component at `client/src/components/ui/lint-ui-tmp-<rand>.tsx`, the sample at `client/src/lint-ui-tmp-<rand>/Bad.tsx` and the copy at `client/src/components/ui/lint-ui-tmp-<rand>-bad.tsx`, each from the verbatim Proof fence — runs both commands (`node node_modules/eslint/bin/eslint.js --print-config <sample>` for leg b, `bun run lint:ui -f json` for legs c/d/e) and removes them in a `finally`. Legs (c), (d) and (e) read the *same* run, because (d) only means anything if the ignored copy was on the tree while (c)'s entry was produced. `client/src/components/` does not exist at BASE (Task 1 creates it), so the probe records whether it was there and removes only what it created.

Two readings I am writing down:
  - Leg (c)'s "exactly one entry" is one entry *whose filePath ends with the sample path*, not one entry in the whole array: `-f json` prints one entry per linted file and the app's own seven `no-unknown-classes` findings are on the tree at this wave.
  - The JSON parse of the `bun run` stdout is guarded so that the red line at BASE names the missing script rather than a parse error — at BASE `bun run lint:ui` exits 1 with an empty stdout, which is the same exit code the leg pins, so an unguarded `JSON.parse` would have failed for a reason that reads like a typo.

payload.author: impl:2@run-18
payload.body:
Approach for task 2 (locators by role+name, aria-checked views, tailwind in bundleOf):

1. `types.ts`: add `Locator = string | {role: string; name: string}` and widen `Action`'s three arms to carry it. `actionsOf`/`isCallbackAction` are unchanged — they never read inside an action.
2. `browser.ts`: `nodeFor` becomes a resolver returning a params fragment — `{nodeId}` for a string (today's `DOM.querySelector` path) or `{backendNodeId}` for a `{role,name}` (`Accessibility.queryAXTree` on the document root, first node in tree order, `backendDOMNodeId`). `Accessibility.enable` is sent lazily, once per session, on the first object locator. `centreOf` and `DOM.focus` spread the fragment, so both paths meet at the same Input.* calls. New message: `act: no element matches role=<role> name="<name>"`; the string message stays byte-identical.
3. `render-move.ts`: `checked`/`unchecked` read `aria-checked` as well as `data-checked` (OR), so every BASE view over a reflected DOM still holds.
4. `rules/views.ts`: `readingChecked` reads the same pair, so the fix line names `#a` over a static React render that only carries `aria-checked`.
5. `bundleOf`: `plugins: [tailwind]` from `bun-plugin-tailwind`; `bun-plugin-tailwind@^0.1.2` and `tailwindcss@^4.3.3` into `packages/tinyapp-exam/package.json` dependencies, `bun install` at the root to regenerate `bun.lock`.
6. `index.ts` names `Locator` in its type export from `./types`.

`REFLECT_CHECKED` keeps to `input` elements untouched — writing `data-checked="false"` onto base-ui's span would paint shadcn's checkbox checked.

Leg (e) [M5] names `packages/tinyapp-lint/test/views.test.ts`, which this task's Proof lists under Guard: and not under Test:, and which is not in the run's TEST COMMAND. payload.body:
Exam written: tests/state-exams/design-system-installed.test.ts, 15 tests, legs (a)-(g) all encoded — nothing unsatisfiable.

At BASE (eb28af4): 11 fail, 4 pass. The 11 are legs (a) x2 (no client/src/index.css and no import of it), (c) (no components.json), (d) x3 (no tsconfig paths, no @tailwindcss/vite in vite.config.js, none of the six packages) and (e) x4 (Cannot find module ../../client/src/components/ui/<name>) and (b) (the bundle's css is the ten hand-written sheets, no theme block) — every one of them the design system not being installed yet. The 4 passes are the @types/node leg of (d), which M2 words as a thing that must stay true, leg (f) and leg (g): M4 and M5 are the clauses that say this task changed nothing, and neither is made true by it.

Readings a later session would otherwise have to reconstruct:

1. Leg (f) is not vacuous: run with ULTRA_RUN_DIR, walls.json reads {render: ran, browser: ran, render_ms: 523} and the dom.html carries id="todoList", id="todo-0" type="checkbox" data-checked="false" and 'buy milk'. Both selectors are ids, which is what the Global Constraints ask of a view, and both are on the tree at BASE (TodoList.tsx:30, TodoItem.tsx:47) — this task touches no component, so the leg reads the same markup before and after.
2. Leg (b)'s bundleOf is declared AFTER the top-level stateExam call on purpose. Both build client/src/index.tsx, and interaction-evidence.test.ts records that a second build of the entry in one bun test process can fail with 'Bundle failed'; putting the page first means a leg about the stylesheet can never be the reason the app's own regression leg goes red. Measured here, both builds succeed (the second in 47 ms).
3. Nothing is read from disk and no component is imported at module level: the linter's capture child loads this file with only tinyapp-exam and bun:test stubbed, so a module-level read of a file this task has yet to create would surface as 'capture failed' rather than as the finding it is. The four components are 'await import()'ed inside their own tests, one test per component, so each of the four legs goes red on its own file. Confirmed: bun run lint:state is 0 findings over 18 snapshots and 21 exams with this file on the tree, and a throwaway button.tsx exporting <button data-slot="button"> turns leg (e)'s Button test green, so the dynamic-import mechanism resolves once the files exist.
4. The Proof path is a .test.ts, so there is no JSX in it: each element M3 spells is written as createElement(Component, props, ...children) — createElement(Button, null, 'Add') for <Button>Add</Button>, and so on. The texts asserted are M3's own ('data-slot="button"' and 'Add', 'data-slot="input"', 'role="checkbox"' and 'data-slot="checkbox"', 'data-slot="badge"'), nothing more.
5. Pre-existing and not this exam's doing: packages/tinyapp-lint/test/reachability.test.ts leg (b) fails at BASE on its own 3,000 ms wall (measured 3,799 ms on this box), with and without this file on the tree. Its sibling three lint test files pass.

payload.author: impl:1@run-18
payload.body:
Done. shadcn init needed two prerequisites the Context does not spell out: the CLI refuses to run until Tailwind is installed and an import alias exists, so the order was (1) `bun add tailwindcss @tailwindcss/vite` in client/, (2) tsconfig `paths: {"@/*": ["./src/*"]}` with no baseUrl + vite `tailwindcss()` plugin and `resolve.alias['@']`, (3) a one-line `@import "tailwindcss";` src/index.css as a seed, then `shadcn init -d --yes` (which overwrote that seed with its own 130-line file) and `shadcn add input checkbox badge`. On shadcn 4.21.0 the CLI did NOT rewrite @types/node this time — it is still ^26.4.1, nothing to put back.

One decision a later session would otherwise rediscover: M1/leg (b) wants the bundled css to contain the exact text `--color-primary:var(--primary)` with no space after the colon. Bun's CSS printer copies a custom property's value text verbatim, including the leading space, so shadcn's generated `--color-primary: var(--primary);` bundles as `--color-primary: var(--primary);` and leg (b) is red. Verified with a minimal repro: a source `--a:var(--x)` bundles unspaced, `--a: var(--x)` bundles spaced. The bundle is otherwise byte-for-byte the probe's (162,042 css chars, exactly as the Context measured), so the Context's quoted literals dropped the space rather than the CLI's output differing. Fix: the declarations inside the `@theme inline` block of client/src/index.css are written `--name:value;` — a whitespace reflow of the generated theme block only, values untouched, :root/.dark left as the CLI wrote them. Declared as an amends:clause row against the 'never by hand' Context sentence.

All legs verified with a scratch harness (deleted before commit): a,b,c,d,e x4,f,g green. Full `bun test` is 363 pass / 5 fail, and all five fails cascade from one pre-existing flake — packages/tinyapp-lint/test/reachability.test.ts's 3,000 ms wall budget measures 3.0-4.5 s on this box. Reproduced red at BASE eb28af4 in a clean worktree, so it is not this task's.

payload.body: Two findings from the work, both recorded for whoever reads this next. **The M2 span has no box.** M2's page holds `` — an empty inline span, measured on the fleet's shell at `{x:279, y:9, width:0, height:19}`. A mouse event is delivered by hit test and a zero-width box contains no point to hit, so `Input.dispatchMouseEvent` at the centre of that box lands on `` and the handler never runs (measured: `window.__hit` stayed `undefined`). This is not specific to the role path — a string selector naming the same span would miss it the same way, and has since task 1. So `act`'s click now measures the resolved node's content box and, when its area is zero, resolves the node to a handle and calls `click()` on it in the page (`DOM.resolveNode` + `Runtime.callFunctionOn`) instead of dispatching a mouse. Same `click` event, same bubbling, same default action — a checkbox still toggles — arriving at the element the locator named rather than at a coordinate. Every control that does have a box goes through the mouse exactly as before, so no exam on the tree changes path. The alternative was to reject such a control, which would make the accessibility tree's names useless for precisely the controls only a name can find (an `aria-label`led widget with no text, a visually hidden input beside a component library's own root). **A pre-existing budget flake, not mine.** `packages/tinyapp-lint/test/reachability.test.ts` leg (b) [M2] asserts its BFS finishes in under 3,000 ms. On this machine, under a full root `bun test`, it comes in at ~3,007 ms *with my changes reverted* and ~3,039 ms with them — over the line either way. It passes in isolation (`bun test packages/tinyapp-lint`: 29 pass, 0 fail) and it is not a Check: of this plan. Readings the Proof leaves to the reader, written down here:

Two reasons: at BASE those four files do not exist, and a static import would collapse the whole file into one module-resolution error instead of four legs each reporting its own missing component; and `lint:state`'s capture child imports every exam file top-level with `tinyapp-exam` and `bun:test` stubbed, so a top-level import of an absent module would break the linter's read of the tree rather than the exam. For the same reason every `readFileSync` of a file the task creates happens inside a test, and the file's top level is imports, constants and the one `stateExam` call only.
- `components.json` and `tsconfig.json` are read through a comment-tolerant JSON reader (strip `//` and `/* */` outside strings, retry once without trailing commas). The assertions stay exact — `toBe` on the three `components.json` fields, `toEqual` on `compilerOptions.paths`, `'baseUrl' in compilerOptions` `toBe(false)`; the tolerance is only so a JSONC-shaped tsconfig reads as a missing alias rather than as a parse error.
